extracted.intended_audience: pr professionals, communications teams, and press-release writers optimizing releases for search engines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and distributing press releases to maximize search visibility, backlinks, and engagement while remaining compliant and reader-focused. Covers on-page SEO, multimedia, distribution channels, tracking, and modern considerations like schema and AI optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword Integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategically place keywords in headline, subheadings, and body
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance: use naturally without overstuffing; Keyword density 1-3% (no more); Include long-tail keyword variants. Keywords should support the message, not dominate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline Optimization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 70 characters for SERP visibility; Front-load most important keywords (first 55 characters); Use power words. Headlines should be both attention-grabbing for humans and optimized for search result display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use links within the release to relevant pages and for SEO value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 2-3 links per 500 words; Don't include links in headlines; Use descriptive anchor text (not "click here"); Link to relevant landing pages; Avoid excessive linking (search engines see as spam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases succeed when human, telling a real story, and useful
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords should support the message, not dominate it; Min 400-500 words for SEO purposes; Original content - don't reuse text from other releases. Focus on readable, newsworthy prose rather than keyword-first copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Include visual and video assets to improve engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include images with alt text; Video improves engagement metrics; Embed metadata in images (e.g., captions, titles, metadata) to aid SEO and reuse. Use alt text for accessibility and to provide additional keyword/context signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution for SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose distribution channels and syndication points to earn backlinks and credibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established newswires for backlinks; Multiple syndication points increase visibility; Distribute through Reg FD-compliant channels for credibility. Prefer reputable networks over low-quality or spammy distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure SEO and distribution outcomes with analytics tools
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SEMrush / Ahrefs / Moz for backlinks and rankings; Google Search Console for impressions and clicks; Newswire analytics for distribution performance. Track both search metrics and syndication backlinks to evaluate ROI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt contemporary formats and signals that impact discovery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobile-first formatting; Structured data / schema markup; Optimize for AI assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI); Voice-search-friendly phrasing. Implement schema and mobile layout to improve how search engines and AI surfaces present the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-Patterns / Things to Avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices that harm SEO, deliverability, or credibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive keyword stuffing; Buying backlinks; Spammy distribution networks; Identical text across multiple releases; Hidden text or hidden links. These can trigger search penalties, reduce credibility, and harm reach.
